customManagers.description: Go release series used to select the pinned compiler image.
Pinned Go compiler image used by CI images and native runners.
The cert-manager release the test scenarios install, anchored on the `renovate:` comment above the constant.
Pinned Node/npm toolchain for CI without changing HAProxy runtime libraries.
HAProxy patch tags and optional digests in dev manifests and CI bases, updated within each supported series alongside the chart.

HAProxy patch versions in charts/haptic/values.yaml. Each entry's series (captured from the YAML key) is baked into a per-dep regex versioning scheme, so Renovate only considers patches within the same series. Adding or removing a series requires no renovate.json change.

SPOA hub bundle versions in versions-spoa.env. Each entry has a `# renovate:` comment naming the upstream GitHub repository whose releases carry the artifacts, optionally followed by free-form `#` notes documenting the bump, then a `<NAME>_VERSION="vX.Y.Z"` assignment. The intermediate `(?:#[^\n]*\n)*` group allows any number of comment lines between the renovate directive and the assignment so the file stays readable as the metric set + behaviour notes grow. The shipped customManagers:gitlabPipelineVersions preset only matches .gitlab-ci.yml so we need a dedicated manager for this file.

Vector sidecar image tag in charts/haptic/values.yaml. The tag carries a distro suffix (e.g. 0.57.0-debian), so the versioning scheme captures the semver part and keeps the suffix out of the comparison; without it Renovate treats the whole string as an unparseable version and never proposes a bump. The `# renovate:` comment must sit directly above the `tag:` line.

Valkey image tag, in every file that pins one, for the same reason as the Varnish manager above: values.yaml was bumped to 9-alpine while the annotation-library default, its snippet fallback, and the e2e preload stayed on 8-alpine. Same comment-anchored pattern — a `renovate:` line immediately above the pin.

Valkey pin as DOCUMENTED in the chart values reference. reference.md is hand-maintained and check-values-docs.sh fails the build when a documented default drifts from values.yaml, so a bot bump that touched only values.yaml reddened every renovate MR until the row was edited by hand (!1515). Matched on the table cell rather than a `renovate:` comment anchor, because the generated-looking rows carry no comments.

HAProxy patch versions in the generated chart defaults. charts/haptic/charts/helm-helpers/files/default-values.json is generated from values.yaml and make lint fails when they differ; this mirrors the values.yaml manager above so a bot bump updates both.

Vector image tag in the generated chart defaults. charts/haptic/charts/helm-helpers/files/default-values.json is generated from values.yaml and make lint fails when they differ; this mirrors the values.yaml manager above so a bot bump updates both.

Valkey image in the generated chart defaults. charts/haptic/charts/helm-helpers/files/default-values.json is generated from values.yaml and make lint fails when they differ; this mirrors the values.yaml manager above so a bot bump updates both.
Vector pin as DOCUMENTED in the chart values reference — same reason as the Valkey entry above (!1985 bumped values.yaml only).
Calico images in the CNI manifest every test Kind cluster installs.
Upstream Calico version in the CNI manifest header; TestCalicoManifest requires it to equal the image tags.

packageRules.description: One automerged PR per week for every non-major update. Renovate only bundles updates it finds in the same run, so the weekly window — not the grouping alone — is what collapses the PR count. A rule that sets its own groupName keeps a separate PR and inherits this schedule.
Packages HAPTIC's maintainers publish skip the soak — minimumReleaseAge guards against a compromised third-party release and buys nothing here, while delaying an internal fix reaching its consumer.
Major updates keep their own MR (:separateMajorReleases in the shared preset) but share its weekly window, so they don't start a full pipeline mid-week. Vulnerability fixes ignore every schedule.

The scriggo runtime is a HAPTIC fork (github.com/haproxy-haptic/scriggo), tracked by the built-in gomod manager as a pseudo-version digest. A digest bump is a fork sync that may carry an upstream security fix, but nothing here links it to open2b/scriggo advisories (govulncheck keys on module path). Force human review — never auto-merge — so a reviewer checks each bump against the upstream advisory watch. See docs/site/docs/development/scriggo-fork-maintenance.md.
Go toolchain bumps share one MR with every vulnerability fix: make audit gates on all of them, so split MRs each fail on the vulns the other fixes.
Group all HAProxy image/patch bumps into a single MR per run

Keep HAPROXY_VERSION ARGs on stable series only. Docker Hub's floating `X.Y` tag can point at a dev release before the first `X.Y.Z` patch ships (e.g. `3.4` → `3.4-dev2`), so derive the tracked version from patch tags. Covers both the `ARG HAPROXY_VERSION=` lines and the `FROM haproxytech/haproxy-debian:${HAPROXY_VERSION}` lines that Renovate's built-in dockerfile manager extracts by resolving the ARG — both need the clamp, across all three files.

Keep HAPROXY_VERSION in the CI image Dockerfile on stable series only. Upstream haproxy/haproxy tags are `vX.Y-devN` during development and `vX.Y.Z` at release; deriving the version from patch tags skips series that have no stable release yet.

Group all SPOA hub bundle bumps (hub + 6 plugins) into a single MR per run so the bundle moves forward atomically. No auto-merge: these bumps re-validate the supply-chain prep job and the smoke test, so a human should review at least until the bundle has been stable for a release cycle.

Ignore the placeholder ARG defaults in the CI image Dockerfiles. They read `<image>:must-be-supplied@sha256:0000...`, are always overridden with --build-arg from ci/build-pins.yml (where the real tag@digest pins live and ARE tracked by the customManagers above), and exist only so a build without the arg fails loudly. Renovate's dockerfile manager reads them as real dependencies and reports `Could not determine new digest` for golang, python and haproxytech/haproxy-debian on every run - permanent Dependency Dashboard noise that hides a genuine lookup failure when one occurs.

k8s.io/kube-openapi has no tagged releases and must move with the k8s.io/apimachinery release that adopts it: a lone digest bump pulled structured-merge-diff/v7 while apimachinery v0.37.0 compiles against v6 and broke build, lint, and test (!1801). The kubernetes group's go mod tidy raises it when apimachinery moves.
Calico's images and manifest header move together in one PR.
A Calico minor or major release changes its CRDs and manifest, which Renovate cannot regenerate.
